item.title: Client-side semantic search for your static site
item.description: This blog now has semantic search that runs entirely in your browser. No server, no API keys, no 23 MB transformer. The whole model is a 4 MB lookup table, and extends the existing keyword search with semantic capabilities.

item.title: Running a coding agent locally for when the budget runs out
item.description: The all-you-can-eat AI coding era is over. So what do you do on the 22nd of the month, when the token budget's gone and there's over a week of work left? Here's a local coding agent (Pi plus Qwen3-Coder on a MacBook) that's decent enough for the routine stuff and runs for free (if you have enough RAM).

item.title: Your OpenClaw can book flights. But can it survive a dungeon crawl?
item.description: Everyone's building AI agents that send emails and book flights. How about one that fights monsters in a dungeon? Here's how you can too.

item.title: Building a semantic search engine in ±250 lines of Python
item.description: Our keyword search engine can't find 'alcoholic beverage disaster in England' even though the London Beer Flood is right there. In this post, we add semantic search using sentence-transformers embeddings and cosine similarity to find documents by meaning, not just matching words.

item.title: Migrating my hopelessly outdated Hugo blog with Claude Code
item.description: I haven't really touched my blog since 2019. The theme was ancient, jQuery was everywhere, and I kept putting off the inevitable migration. Then I decided to let an LLM do it. Here's what happened when Claude Code spent an evening trying to modernize my setup.
